muse_spark_1.3/001: The strategy is negamax search with Clobber bitboards, mobility evaluation and time controlled iterative deepening.
muse_spark_1.3/002: The strategy is iterative-deepening negamax with alpha-beta, transposition table and time control. Boards are bitboards (30 bits) with precomputed neighbours. All moves are captures that create a permanent empty, so the game is acyclic and splits into components. Move count is symmetric for both sides, so the evaluation uses number of movable/vulnerable pieces difference, total contact count as tempo, and centrality weights, preferring central moves that minimise opponent mobility. Root moves are ordered centrally and reordered by previous iteration. Mate scores force wins and delay losses. Search aborts on timeout and always falls back to a legal move.
muse_spark_1.3/003: The strategy combines exact search in the endgame with selective search and Monte Carlo evaluation in the opening. Clobber on 5x6 always reduces total stones, adjacency is symmetric so static mobility is equal for both sides, therefore the leaf value is mobility plus centrality and minimax naturally minimises the opponent's next mobility. Move ordering prefers central captures, iterative deepening alpha-beta with transposition table gives a principal variation, and remaining time is used for flat UCB Monte Carlo with uniform random playouts to correct the heuristic when branching is ~49. The best win-rate move is played, guaranteeing a legal capture.
muse_spark_1.3/004: The strategy is Clobber specific search. White to move and Black to move have the same number of captures because every adjacent You-Opponent edge is a move for both sides, so material and mobility difference are zero. Strength comes from leaving the opponent with minimal future mobility. The board is encoded in 30-bit integers for speed, captures are generated with neighbour masks and popcount, terminal loss is mate scoring with distance, leaf score is mobility plus centralisation. Root moves are ordered by opponent evaluation, inner nodes by central heuristic plus transposition-table best move. Iterative deepening negamax with alpha-beta, transposition table and time control searches as deep as possible in ~0.85s and always returns a legal capture.
muse_spark_1.3/005: The strategy is built for the impartial Clobber game. Board is kept as two 30-bit bitboards, neighbours precomputed, move generation by bit operations. Immediate wins are taken. Small endgames are solved exactly by depth-first win/loss search with memoisation on unordered positions and time abort. Otherwise moves are ordered by 1-ply opponent mobility - fewer opponent moves is better - and refined by Monte-Carlo random playouts from each root move in round-robin until ~0.93s expires. The move with highest simulated win-rate, tie-broken by low opponent mobility, is played. All paths guarantee a legal `'row,col,dir'` return.
